question: The vertices of $\triangle ABC$ are $A(1,1)$, $B(7,3)$, and $C(3,9)$. If $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$, use determinants to calculate the areas of $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle ACD$, establish that $AD$ divides $\triangle ABC$ into two triangles of equal area, and hence obtain the area of $\triangle ABC$.
explanation:
Coordinates of the midpoint
Since $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$,
$$D=\left(\frac{7+3}{2},\frac{3+9}{2}\right)=(5,6)$$

Area of the first triangle
Using the determinant formula,
$$\text{Area of }\triangle ABD=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\7 & 3 & 1\\5 & 6 & 1\end{vmatrix}\right|$$
$$=\frac{1}{2}|1(3-6)-1(7-5)+(42-15)|$$
$$=\frac{1}{2}|-3-2+27|=\frac{1}{2}(22)=11$$

Area of the second triangle
$$\text{Area of }\triangle ACD=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\3 & 9 & 1\\5 & 6 & 1\end{vmatrix}\right|$$
$$=\frac{1}{2}|1(9-6)-1(3-5)+(18-45)|$$
$$=\frac{1}{2}|3+2-27|=\frac{1}{2}(22)=11$$
Therefore,
$$\text{Area of }\triangle ABD=\text{Area of }\triangle ACD$$
Thus, the median $AD$ divides $\triangle ABC$ into two triangles of equal area.

Area of the original triangle
$$\text{Area of }\triangle ABC=11+11=22$$
Hence, the area of $\triangle ABC$ is $22$ square units.

options.A: $D=(5,6)$; $[\triangle ABD]=22$ square units and $[\triangle ACD]=22$ square units; therefore $[\triangle ABC]=44$ square units
options.B: $D=(5,6)$; $[\triangle ABD]=11$ square units and $[\triangle ACD]=9$ square units; therefore $AD$ does not divide the triangle into equal areas
options.C: $D=(5,6)$; $[\triangle ABD]=11$ square units and $[\triangle ACD]=11$ square units; therefore $AD$ divides $\triangle ABC$ into two equal-area triangles and $[\triangle ABC]=22$ square units
options.D: $D=(4,6)$; $[\triangle ABD]=10$ square units and $[\triangle ACD]=10$ square units; therefore $[\triangle ABC]=20$ square units
